_comment: The Grade 4 Global Perspectives standalone lesson build, described for ../../mathematics/lesson-app-tools and built by ../lesson-kit. Order here IS the lesson number. Eight lessons organised by the six skills of Cambridge Primary Global Perspectives 0838 Stage 4 (18 objectives - Cambridge publishes ONE set for Stages 3 to 4, so these are the Stage 3 objectives under 4… codes, and the difference from Grade 3 is the topics and the depth, not new machines), each anchored on one topic an eight-to-nine-year-old can investigate, NOT by the units of the Word-pack course under global-perspectives/grade-4/data, so progress is written under l01..l08 - see THE UNIT PROBLEM in wire-progress.py. objectiveFloors are recorded at the measured value after each build and may rise, not fall.
subject: global-perspectives
hubStrands: Constructing our own questions to understand a topic; locating the information and the answers inside a source; investigating by questionnaire, observation and measurement; and selecting, organising and recording what we found in charts and diagrams.

Knowing that people think and believe different things about a topic; drawing conclusions from charts and numbers; talking about the causes of what we do and its consequences for others; and suggesting actions that could make a difference to an issue affecting other people.
Discussing a source and seeing that its author has a viewpoint; and giving an opinion about somebody else's viewpoint, with reasons.

Saying what we did well in a team and what we could do better; saying how working together made the outcome better; saying what we learned and how our ideas changed; and saying which kinds of activity help us learn.
Giving out the team's jobs so each goes to the right person; and bringing ideas to the team while working positively with everyone in it.
Presenting information about a topic clearly, with a start, a middle and an end; and listening to others, then responding with relevant ideas and questions.
